reviewer: maintainer with LLM-assisted review per ADR-0018; metrics read from review-queue.selected.json
notes: Queue built from the --candidate-limit 20000 run because the production cap (100) suppresses 1,598 of 1,698 qualifying cells and the queue module derives cap suppression from score rank vs the production cap. Evaluation is run against the production top-100 (deterministic score-desc/scopeId-asc rank <= 100). Adversarial depth on all 26 emitted cells (including cap-suppressed controls), light on the 16 clean/skipped controls. A month-long stop-direction-hour cell at 5-10 scheduled buses/hour should yield roughly 100-200+ observed headways; cells with 10-25 observed headways have fractional GTFS-RT coverage, so very large EWT values there are treated as feed-gap artifacts, not service findings.

decisions.rationale: Rank 1 in the production cap. EWT 18.1 min vs 6 min scheduled wait, CoV 2.16, LoS F — but only 21 observed headways across a month of weekday hour-7 service at 5 scheduled buses/hour (~110 expected). Coverage is too fractional to separate real morning unreliability from feed gaps; needs more observed coverage before any promotion.

Claims 78.3 min of excess wait against a 6 min scheduled wait (CoV 6.95) from only 23 observed headways. A month-typical 78-minute wait at 5 scheduled buses/hour is implausible as service; the magnitude is driven by hour-plus gaps in sparse GTFS-RT coverage being read as headways. Feed-gap artifact, not a publishable claim. This cell IS in the production top-100 — recorded as suppress leakage, not relabeled.

EWT 9.5 min, CoV 1.46, 25 observed headways — the most plausible of the B11 trio, but still ~25 of ~110 expected weekday hour-6 headways. The moderate magnitude is believable; the sample is not yet. Hold for more coverage.
EWT 18.4 min, CoV 2.58, 21 observed headways at 5 scheduled buses/hour. Same pattern as B11 hour-7: plausible direction, fractional coverage, cannot rule out feed-gap inflation of the tail.

EWT 30.4 min (CoV 3.42) from only 10 observed headways — the detector's absolute minimum — for a month of weekday hour-9 service at 6 scheduled buses/hour (~130 expected). At ~8% coverage a single feed gap dominates the estimate. In the production top-100 — counted as suppress leakage.

Hour-4 (4am) cell with EWT 8.0 min, barely above plausible-noise for overnight service, 14 observed headways, and a suspicious 6.3 scheduled buses/hour at 4am that suggests schedule-data noise. Keep visible to reviewers as an overnight-schedule data-quality probe, not a rider-facing claim.
EWT 10.9 min, CoV 1.86, but 13 observed headways for a month of hour-6 service at 6 scheduled buses/hour. Believable magnitude, unusable sample size.

Another 4am cell (EWT 20.9 min, 16 headways, scheduled headway 12 min). Overnight cells mix layover/pull-out behavior with sparse feed coverage; the cluster of B15 hour-4 emissions looks like a structural overnight artifact rather than three independent findings. Reviewer-only pending an overnight-hours gate decision.

Adjacent stop to B15:301123 in the same hour-4 window with near-identical metrics (EWT 20.2 vs 20.9, 14 headways) — these are one upstream event/coverage pattern surfacing at consecutive stops, not independent cells. Same overnight-artifact concern; reviewer-only.
Saturday hour-19 cell: EWT 10.9 min at 8 scheduled buses/hour but only 10 observed headways across ~4 Saturdays (~35 expected). Minimum-sample emission; magnitude plausible, evidence thin.

Cap-suppressed (rank 101). Claims 60.4 min excess wait against a 3 min scheduled wait (CoV 8.61) from 10 observed headways on Saturday evenings at 10 scheduled buses/hour. A 60-minute typical wait on a 6-minute-headway corridor is a feed-gap reading, not service.

Cap-suppressed. EWT 88.8 min (CoV 9.31) from 12 observed headways at SURF AV/W 32 ST — the Coney Island terminal end of the B36 — in hour 6. Terminal pull-outs plus near-empty feed coverage produce hour-scale phantom headways. Artifact.

Cap-suppressed express cell: EWT 21.8 min, CoV 1.85, 15 observed headways at exactly the 5 buses/hour frequency floor. Express PM-peak unreliability into Brooklyn is plausible, but at the frequency floor the frequent-service EWT framing is fragile and the sample is half the high-confidence bar.
Cap-suppressed: EWT 10.5 min, CoV 1.77, 16 observed headways at 6 scheduled buses/hour in the AM peak. Plausible but under-sampled; hold.
Cap-suppressed Grand Concourse cell: EWT 11.8 min, CoV 1.92, 13 observed headways of ~120 expected at 5.4 buses/hour. Magnitude credible for the corridor, coverage fractional.

Cap-suppressed: EWT 15.8 min, CoV 2.03, 11 observed headways — one above the minimum gate. Same BX1 corridor as the hour-9 cell, which adds plausibility, but each cell individually is too thin to promote.

Cap-suppressed express cell on Lexington Av: EWT 9.0 min, CoV 1.02 (the tamest variability in the selected set), 12 observed headways. Closest to an ordinary moderate shortfall, but the sample is too thin and the EWT is near the bottom of the emitted range.

Six blocks from BXM1:402838 in the same hour with near-identical metrics (EWT 8.8 vs 9.0, 13 headways) — consecutive-stop duplication of one upstream pattern. Same hold-for-evidence call; a future rollup should dedupe consecutive-stop cells before any route claim.

Cap-suppressed: claims 34.9 min excess wait at 11.6 scheduled buses/hour — but only 12 observed headways where ~250 are expected (~5% coverage). At that coverage the EWT is measuring feed gaps on Madison Av, not service. Artifact.

Cap-suppressed: EWT 17.4 min, CoV 3.08 at 7 scheduled buses/hour — a CoV of 3 implies ~21-minute headway swings on a 7-minute-headway corridor, which from 14 observed headways (~150 expected) is as consistent with feed gaps as with bunching. Keep for reviewers as an ambiguous case; not publishable either way yet.

Cap-suppressed at rank 593. EWT 12.9 min vs 5.8 min scheduled wait, CoV 1.79, with 30 observed headways — exactly the detector's own high-confidence sample bar. The magnitude is moderate and internally consistent (average wait 18.6 min at a 10-min scheduled headway), not gap-shaped. Best-evidenced Queens cell in the queue; survives adversarial read as a descriptive cell-level claim. Confidence medium because 30 headways is the bar, not comfortably above it.
decisions.notes: Suppressed by the production top-100 cap. Counted against primary survival — this is the cap-bias finding, not a labeling adjustment.

decisions.rationale: Cap-suppressed: claims 98.8 min excess wait (CoV 10.34) from 10 observed headways on Saturday hour-19 service at 9 scheduled buses/hour. The largest EWT in the selected set on the thinnest possible sample — a textbook feed-gap reading.

Cap-suppressed at rank 1131. EWT 10.7 min, CoV 1.37, 45 observed headways (1.5x the high-confidence bar) at the Water St/John St express pickup in the AM peak. Metrics are internally consistent and the moderate magnitude fits known express-bus AM variability into the Financial District. Tagged borderline_frequency because the 5 scheduled buses/hour sits at the frequency floor where the frequent-service EWT framing is weakest — that is a readiness gate to track, not a disqualifier on this evidence.
decisions.notes: Suppressed by the production top-100 cap; counts against primary survival.

decisions.rationale: Cap-suppressed: EWT 94.1 min with CoV 18.65 — the most extreme variability in the set — from 18 observed headways near the St. George ferry terminal end of the S40 in hour 6. Terminal-adjacent geometry plus sparse coverage; not a service claim.

Cap-suppressed at rank 1310. The best-sampled emitted cell in the entire queue: 69 observed headways (2.3x the high-confidence bar) at Greenwich St/Battery Pl in hour 7, EWT 18.1 min vs 4.3 min scheduled wait, CoV 3.14. With this sample density the variability is service (SI express arrivals bunching through Lower Manhattan in the AM peak), not feed gaps. Survives adversarial read as a descriptive cell-level claim.
decisions.notes: Suppressed by the production top-100 cap; counts against primary survival. The single strongest example of the cap-bias cost.

decisions.rationale: Cap-suppressed: EWT 21.8 min, CoV 3.78, 13 observed headways at 6.3 scheduled buses/hour. Express AM-peak unreliability is plausible (cf. QM11/SIM1) but this cell lacks their sample support; hold for more coverage.
Clean control: passed all readiness gates (10 headways, 8 buses/hour) and scored below the emission threshold. Nothing in the cell contradicts the no-hit outcome.
Clean control on an SBS corridor: 10 headways at 8 buses/hour, below threshold. Correctly quiet.

Clean control one hour before the two emitted BXM1 hour-8 cells, at the 5 buses/hour frequency floor with 11 headways. Useful contrast showing the hour-8 emissions are hour-specific; suppress is correct for this cell.
Clean control: 10 headways at 10 buses/hour Saturday evening, below threshold. Correctly quiet.

Clean control on the same route as the suppressed Q17 Saturday hour-19 artifact, one hour later and the opposite direction, with the same 10-headway sample but no inflated EWT. Reinforces that the hour-19 emission was a localized gap reading, not route-wide Saturday collapse.

Clean control with strong sampling (57 headways) at the 5 buses/hour floor — a well-observed express cell that genuinely ran reliably. Good negative example pairing with QM11's well-observed positive.
Clean control at hour 5 with 10 headways at 5.2 buses/hour; below threshold. Correctly quiet.
Clean control: SI express hour-5 cell with 15 headways at the frequency floor, below threshold. Correctly quiet.
Skipped control (insufficient_headways): a single observed headway at Saturday midnight. The skip gate is doing exactly its job.
Skipped control: 2 observed headways in the weekday AM peak on an express route. Correctly skipped; also a reminder that BM1's emitted cells sit just above this coverage cliff.
Skipped control (insufficient_headways, 1 headway). Correct.
Skipped control (insufficient_headways, 1 headway on a Saturday express cell). Correct.

Skipped control on a shuttle/non-revenue route id (J90) at Saturday midnight with 1 headway. Correctly skipped; J90/L90 shuttle ids in the universe are a denominator-hygiene note for the fleet-universe enumeration.

Skipped control (baseline_unavailable) with 57 observed headways — a well-observed shuttle cell with no schedule baseline to compare against. The skip is correct: EWT is undefined without a scheduled-wait baseline.
Skipped control (insufficient_headways, 2 headways). Correct.
